description: Testing standards for quality assurance - naming, coverage, and patterns

naming.description: Test file and function naming conventions

rules.description: Test files must use .test. or .spec. naming
rules.message: Test files should use .test.ts or .spec.ts naming

rules.description: Test files should have describe blocks
rules.message: Organize tests with describe() blocks

rules.description: Test names should be descriptive
rules.message: Use descriptive test names that explain the expected behavior

rules.description: Test names should start with 'should'
rules.message: Consider starting test names with 'should' for clarity

rules.description: Tests should follow Arrange-Act-Assert pattern
rules.message: Structure tests with clear Arrange, Act, and Assert sections
rules.design_check: Does the testing strategy describe Arrange-Act-Assert structure for tests?

rules.description: Tests should have a single logical assertion
rules.message: Consider splitting tests with multiple assertions

rules.description: Tests should not depend on each other
rules.message: Tests should be independent and run in any order
rules.design_check: Does the testing design ensure tests are independent and can run in any order? Flag any design that implies test ordering.

rules.description: Tests should clean up after themselves
rules.message: Use afterEach/afterAll for cleanup

rules.description: Minimum code coverage threshold
rules.message: Code coverage is below threshold
rules.design_check: Does the plan specify minimum coverage thresholds (lines: 70%, branches: 60%, functions: 70%)? If missing, add coverage requirements to the definition of done.

rules.description: Mock external service calls in unit tests
rules.message: External services should be mocked in unit tests
rules.design_check: Does the design identify which external dependencies (APIs, DBs, queues) will be mocked in unit tests? Specify mocking strategy early.

rules.description: Avoid excessive mocking
rules.message: Too many mocks may indicate test is too coupled to implementation

rules.description: Restore mocks after tests
rules.message: Ensure mocks are restored with jest.restoreAllMocks()

rules.description: Use realistic mock data
rules.message: Use factories or fixtures for realistic test data

rules.description: Tests must have assertions
rules.message: Tests must have at least one assertion

rules.description: Use specific assertions over generic ones
rules.message: Use specific assertions like toEqual(), toContain()

rules.description: Async tests must use await or return promise
rules.message: Async tests must await assertions or return the promise

rules.description: Tests must not rely on unseeded randomness
rules.message: Mock or seed randomness to make tests deterministic (faker.js with faker.seed() is acceptable)

rules.description: Retries allowed only for known flaky tests
rules.message: Retries should be limited and documented

rules.description: No skipped tests in CI
rules.message: Skipped tests should be temporary and documented

testing_anti_patterns.description: Common testing mistakes and what NOT to do

rules.description: NEVER test implementation details instead of behavior
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Testing implementation details makes tests brittle. Test behavior and outcomes, not internal mechanics.

rules.description: AVOID excessive snapshot testing
rules.message: CAUTION: Snapshots are easily approved without review. Use for stable UI components only, not logic. Test specific assertions instead.

rules.description: AVOID mocking everything - test real interactions where possible
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Excessive mocking tests the mocks, not the code. Mock external dependencies, not your own modules.

rules.description: NEVER test framework/library behavior
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Don't test that React renders components or Express creates routes. Test YOUR behavior on top of libraries.

rules.description: AVOID generic test names like 'test that it works'
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Vague test names hide what's being tested. Describe the specific behavior: 'should return 404 when user not found'.

rules.description: AVOID multiple unrelated assertions in one test
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Multiple unrelated assertions make it unclear what failed. One logical assertion per test.

rules.description: AVOID hiding test setup in beforeAll that affects understanding
rules.message: CAUTION: Complex beforeAll setup hides test dependencies. Keep setup close to tests that need it for clarity.

rules.description: NEVER share mutable state between tests
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Shared mutable state causes test order dependencies and flakiness. Create fresh state in each test.

rules.description: NEVER use fixed sleep/delays in tests
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Fixed delays make tests slow and flaky. Use waitFor, polling, or mock timers instead.

rules.description: NEVER ignore promise rejections in tests
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Empty catch handlers hide failures. Let tests fail on unexpected errors.

rules.description: AVOID conditional logic in tests
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Conditional logic in tests hides which path was tested. Split into separate tests for each case.

rules.description: AVOID testing trivial getters and setters
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Testing trivial getters/setters tests JavaScript, not your code. Test meaningful behavior.

rules.description: AVOID exact string matching for error messages
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Exact error message matching breaks on rewording. Use toMatch or toContain for key phrases.

rules.description: AVOID hardcoding database IDs in tests
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Hardcoded IDs couple tests to database state. Use factory-created entities or test the ID's existence.

rules.description: AVOID testing against real system clock
rules.message: ANTI-PATTERN: Tests against real time are flaky. Use fake timers or inject a clock abstraction.
